edits.source_excerpt: Let $(f,X)$ be Morse--Smale on an $n$-manifold.  For distinct critical points $p,q$, $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(p,q)$ is a smooth manifold of dimension $\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)$ (and is empty if the transverse fibre product is empty).
edits.proposed_replacement: Let $(f,X)$ be Morse--Smale on an $n$-manifold. For distinct critical points $p,q$, $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(p,q)$ is a smooth manifold, possibly empty. When nonempty, it has dimension $\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)$. If $\lambda(p)<\lambda(q)$, it is empty.

edits.source_excerpt: [F2] A transverse fibre product of smooth maps is an embedded submanifold of the product ([[thm-transverse-fibre-product-theorem]]).
edits.proposed_replacement: [F2] For transverse smooth maps $F:A\to N$ and $G:B\to N$, their fibre product is an embedded submanifold of $A\times B$, possibly empty. When nonempty, each component has dimension $\dim A+\dim B-\dim N$; in particular it is empty if this difference is negative ([[thm-transverse-fibre-product-theorem]]).

edits.source_excerpt: 2.1 The dimension of that transverse fibre product is $\lambda(p)+(n-\lambda(q))-n=\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)$ by [F1]. [F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
edits.proposed_replacement: 2.1 First suppose $\lambda(p)<\lambda(q)$. The source dimensions in [F1] sum to $\lambda(p)+(n-\lambda(q))<n$, so [F2] makes the fibre product empty. If the fibre product is nonempty, [F2] instead gives its dimension as $\lambda(p)+(n-\lambda(q))-n=\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)\ge0$. These cases prove the stated conditional dimension and emptiness assertions without assigning a negative dimension to an empty space. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra, cases] ∎

records.rationale: Conditional nonempty dimension and empty negative-index case; proof splits before dimension formula.
point_of_use_dimensions: dim W^u(p)=λ(p), dim W^s(q)=n−λ(q), ambient target dimension n. If λ(p)+(n−λ(q))<n, transverse fibreproduct empty; otherwise nonempty dimension λ(p)−λ(q).

edits.source_excerpt: [F1] The parametrized space is a smooth manifold of dimension $\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)$ ([[prop-parametrized-morse-trajectory-space-is-a-manifold]]).
edits.proposed_replacement: [F1] The parametrized space is a smooth manifold, possibly empty; when nonempty its dimension is $\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)$, and a negative index difference forces emptiness ([[prop-parametrized-morse-trajectory-space-is-a-manifold]]).

edits.source_excerpt: [F2] A regular intermediate level gives one representative of each time orbit ([[lem-evaluation-on-a-regular-level-identifies-unparametrized-trajectories]]).
edits.proposed_replacement:
[F2] Parametrized trajectories are full nonconstant flow lines with the specified critical endpoint limits, evaluation at zero identifies them with the point-marked stable/unstable intersection, and $df(X)<0$ off the critical set ([[def-parametrized-morse-trajectory-space]], [[def-downward-gradient-like-vector-field]]). The uniqueness-of-level-representative argument in steps 1.1–2.1 of [[lem-evaluation-on-a-regular-level-identifies-unparametrized-trajectories]] uses only continuity, endpoint limits and strict decrease; that bijection argument is repeated below without assuming ambient regularity of the chosen value.

[F3] Stable and unstable manifolds are flow invariant, and their smooth immersion charts are transported local-disk charts; the global flow is jointly smooth. These charts give a smooth time-translation action on their transverse fibre product and a smooth evaluation map ([[lem-stable-and-unstable-manifolds-are-flow-invariant]], [[thm-global-stable-and-unstable-manifolds-are-immersed-euclidean-spaces]], [[thm-fundamental-theorem-on-flows]], [[thm-transverse-fibre-product-theorem]]).

[F4] A nonempty fibre of a smooth map at a regular value is an embedded submanifold of the source with codimension equal to the target dimension ([[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]).

[F5] A scalar equation with nonzero time derivative has a locally unique smooth hitting time, with all finite-dimensional variables retained as parameters ([[thm-parametrized-implicit-function-theorem-with-higher-regularity]]).

edits.source_excerpt: 1.1 Choose a regular $c$ strictly between $f(q)$ and $f(p)$.  The map $f$ restricted to $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(p,q)$ has nonzero derivative along the flow direction, since $df(X)<0$ away from critical points.  Hence its $c$-level is a codimension-one smooth submanifold. [F1, given, algebra]
edits.proposed_replacement: 1.1 Put $P=\widetilde{\mathcal M}(p,q)$. If $P=\varnothing$, its orbit set $\mathcal M(p,q)$ is empty and has the empty smooth structure; no dimension is assigned by a negative formula. Assume henceforth that $P$ is nonempty. No point of a trajectory is critical: flow uniqueness would then make it constant, contradicting its distinct endpoint limits. In the transported immersion charts of [F3], the action $t\cdot\gamma=\gamma(\,\cdot+t)$ is smooth and evaluates to $\Phi_t(\gamma(0))$. Its tangent vector $V$ on the fibre product evaluates to $X(\gamma(0))\ne0$, so $V$ is nonzero. Hence the dimension of the nonempty smooth manifold $P$ is at least one. By [F1], this dimension is $\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)$; in particular an index difference at most zero forces $P$, and therefore its orbit set, to be empty. [F1, F2, F3, given, cases]

edits.source_excerpt: 2.1 By [F2], that level is bijective to $\mathcal M(p,q)$; transport its smooth structure across this bijection.  Its dimension is $\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)-1$ by [F1] and step 1.1. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
edits.proposed_replacement:
1.2 In the nonempty case strict decrease and the endpoint limits imply $f(p)>f(q)$. Set $c=(f(p)+f(q))/2$, without imposing any global regular-value condition on the ambient function $f$, and put $h=f\circ\operatorname{ev}_0:P\to\mathbb R$. This map is smooth by [F3]. For every $\gamma\in P$, the flow tangent vector of step 1.1 satisfies $dh_\gamma(V)=df_{\gamma(0)}(X)<0$, so $h$ is a submersion. For each trajectory, continuity and its two endpoint limits give a finite time $t_0$ with $f(\gamma(t_0))=c$, and strict decrease makes $t_0$ unique. In particular $h^{-1}(c)$ is nonempty. Apply [F4] to $h$, whose scalar target has dimension one: this slice is an embedded codimension-one submanifold of $P$, of dimension $\lambda(p)-\lambda(q)-1\ge0$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Translating each trajectory by its unique time $t_0$ from step 1.2 gives exactly one representative in $h^{-1}(c)$. Conversely, two representatives in the same time orbit can both lie in that slice only if their translation is zero. This is the level-representative bijection, using only the continuity and strict-decrease part of [F2]. Transport the smooth structure of the nonempty slice across its bijection with $\mathcal M(p,q)$. It has the stated dimension by step 1.2. Any other $c'$ strictly between the endpoint values gives the same smooth structure: the equation $h(t\cdot\gamma)=c'$ has nonzero derivative in $t$, so [F5] makes the unique hitting time smooth locally on the first slice; uniqueness patches these local times, and the smooth flow action gives mutually inverse smooth change-of-slice maps. Thus the construction and the empty case prove the full statement without Sard's theorem, an ambient regular level, or an added choice hypothesis. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, construct] ∎

records.rationale: Empty case first, nonzero intrinsic flow tangent forces positive parametrized dimension. Midpoint is regular for the trajectory-height restriction, whose nonempty scalar slice has codimension1. Unique representative and smooth slice transitions use no ambient regular value, Sard, or choice.
point_of_use_dimensions: Nonzero flow tangent forces nonempty parametrized dimension k=λ(p)−λ(q)≥1.
h=f∘ev₀:P^k→R is a submersion, midpoint fibre nonempty, regular-level codim1≤k; nonempty moduli dimension k−1.

edits.source_excerpt: 4. the unparametrized moduli space $\mathcal M(x,y)$, of dimension $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)-1$, is oriented by the flow-first convention on $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma\oplus T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$ ([[def-product-orientation]]), the line $\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma$ carrying the positive flow orientation.
edits.proposed_replacement: 4. the unparametrized moduli space $\mathcal M(x,y)$ is smooth, possibly empty, and when nonempty has dimension $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)-1$ and is oriented by the flow-first convention on $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma\oplus T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$ ([[def-product-orientation]]), the line $\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma$ carrying the positive flow orientation. Empty parametrized or unparametrized spaces carry their unique empty orientation; the orientation-reversal assertions are pointwise.

edits.source_excerpt: [F6] Evaluation at $0$ is a bijection of $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ onto $W^u(x)\cap W^s(y)$; the parametrized space is a smooth manifold of dimension $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)$ with the intersection smooth structure, the transverse fibre product is an embedded submanifold, and $\operatorname{ev}_0(t\cdot\gamma)=\Phi_t(\operatorname{ev}_0(\gamma))$ ([[def-parametrized-morse-trajectory-space]], [[prop-parametrized-morse-trajectory-space-is-a-manifold]], [[thm-transverse-fibre-product-theorem]]).
edits.proposed_replacement: [F6] Evaluation at $0$ is a bijection of $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ onto $W^u(x)\cap W^s(y)$; the parametrized space is a smooth manifold, possibly empty, with dimension $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)$ when nonempty and with the intersection smooth structure; the transverse fibre product is an embedded submanifold, with dimension asserted only when nonempty, and $\operatorname{ev}_0(t\cdot\gamma)=\Phi_t(\operatorname{ev}_0(\gamma))$ ([[def-parametrized-morse-trajectory-space]], [[prop-parametrized-morse-trajectory-space-is-a-manifold]], [[thm-transverse-fibre-product-theorem]]).

edits.source_excerpt: [F8] For $f(y)<c<f(x)$ a regular value, evaluation identifies $\mathcal M(x,y)$ with $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)\cap f^{-1}(c)$, a smooth manifold of dimension $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)-1$, and at a trajectory $\gamma$ the tangent space of the parametrized space splits as $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma\oplus T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$, the first line generated by the nonzero flow vector $\dot\gamma$ ([[thm-unparametrized-trajectory-space-is-a-smooth-manifold]], [[lem-evaluation-on-a-regular-level-identifies-unparametrized-trajectories]]).
edits.proposed_replacement: [F8] The unparametrized space is smooth, possibly empty; when nonempty, its dimension is $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)-1$ and $f(y)<f(x)$. For any $c$ strictly between those endpoint values, the height restriction to the parametrized trajectory manifold is a submersion, and its nonempty $c$-slice gives one representative of each time orbit. No ambient regular-value condition on $f$ is needed for this slice construction. At a representative $\gamma$ on the slice the tangent space splits as $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma\oplus T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$, the first line generated by the nonzero flow vector $\dot\gamma$ ([[thm-unparametrized-trajectory-space-is-a-smooth-manifold]]; the level-representative bijection argument is also in [[lem-evaluation-on-a-regular-level-identifies-unparametrized-trajectories]], Proof 1.1–2.1).

edits.source_excerpt: 5.1 Now assume $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)=1$. By [F6] the identification with the transverse intersection gives $\dim\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\lambda(x)+(n-\lambda(y))-n=1$, and no point of $W^u(x)\cap W^s(y)$ is critical, so the flow vector $X$ is nowhere zero on the one-manifold $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$. Let $L$ be an orbit of the flow. The orbit map $t\mapsto t\cdot\gamma$ is injective by [F9], so $L$ is the injective continuous image of $\mathbb R$; it is open in $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$, since near any of its points a flow box for the nowhere-zero field $X$ (existence and uniqueness for the flow, [F2]) exhibits the local orbits as the connected components of a small chart; and it is closed, because a limit point in $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ of points of $L$ lies on the same local orbit as they do, hence in $L$. A nonempty subset of a manifold that is open, closed and connected is a connected component, so each component of $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ is exactly one flow line. Its tangent space at any point is the line $\mathbb R\cdot X$, and the comparison of the orientation of step 4.1 with the positive flow ray $\mathbb R_{>0}\cdot X$ is locally constant by [F7]; on the connected component this comparison is therefore a constant sign $\epsilon(\gamma)\in\{+1,-1\}$, which is the asserted comparison sign. [F2, F6, F7, F9, step 4.1]

Otherwise, by [F6] the identification with the transverse intersection gives $\dim\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\lambda(x)+(n-\lambda(y))-n=1$, and no point of $W^u(x)\cap W^s(y)$ is critical, so the flow vector $X$ is nowhere zero on the one-manifold $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$. Let $L$ be an orbit of the flow. The orbit map $t\mapsto t\cdot\gamma$ is injective by [F9], so $L$ is the injective continuous image of $\mathbb R$; it is open in $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$, since near any of its points a flow box for the nowhere-zero field $X$ (existence and uniqueness for the flow, [F2]) exhibits the local orbits as the connected components of a small chart; and it is closed, because a limit point in $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ of points of $L$ lies on the same local orbit as they do, hence in $L$. A nonempty subset of a manifold that is open, closed and connected is a connected component, so each component of $\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ is exactly one flow line. Its tangent space at any point is the line $\mathbb R\cdot X$, and the comparison of the orientation of step 4.1 with the positive flow ray $\mathbb R_{>0}\cdot X$ is locally constant by [F7]; on the connected component this comparison is therefore a constant sign $\epsilon(\gamma)\in\{+1,-1\}$, which is the asserted comparison sign. [F2, F6, F7, F9, step 4.1]

edits.source_excerpt: 5.2 It remains to orient the quotient $\mathcal M(x,y)$ of dimension $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)-1$. For a trajectory $\gamma$, choose a regular value $c$ with $f(y)<c<f(x)$; by [F8] the tangent space of the parametrized space splits canonically as $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma\oplus T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$ with $\dot\gamma=X(\gamma(0))$ nonzero, and the orientation of the first summand is the positive flow orientation. By the ordered product isomorphism of [F5] the orientation of $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ from step 4.1 determines a unique ray in $\det T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$, namely the ray whose tensor product with the positive flow ray is the intersection orientation. This ray varies smoothly with $\gamma$ because the splitting and both given orientations do, so it is an orientation of $\mathcal M(x,y)$; the flow-first convention names this choice, and it does not depend on the auxiliary regular value $c$, since the quotient tangent space is the same for every level representative. [F5, F8, step 4.1]
edits.proposed_replacement: 5.2 If $\mathcal M(x,y)$ is empty, give it its unique empty orientation. Otherwise [F8] gives its dimension $\lambda(x)-\lambda(y)-1\ge0$. For a trajectory $\gamma$, choose $c=(f(y)+f(x))/2$ and its representative on that height slice; by [F8] the tangent space of the parametrized space splits canonically as $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)=\mathbb R\cdot\dot\gamma\oplus T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$ with $\dot\gamma=X(\gamma(0))$ nonzero, and the orientation of the first summand is the positive flow orientation. By the ordered product isomorphism of [F5] the orientation of $T_\gamma\widetilde{\mathcal M}(x,y)$ from step 4.1 determines a unique ray in $\det T_\gamma\mathcal M(x,y)$, namely the ray whose tensor product with the positive flow ray is the intersection orientation. This ray varies smoothly with $\gamma$ because the splitting and both given orientations do, so it is an orientation of $\mathcal M(x,y)$; the flow-first convention names this choice, and it does not depend on the auxiliary intermediate value $c$, since the smooth change-of-slice maps of [F8] identify the same quotient tangent space for every level representative. [F5, F8, step 4.1]

At each actual trajectory, the exact flow-first tangent decomposition has dimensions k=1+(k−1); all determinant order and reversal signs unchanged.
